articles.summary: EMVCo released a draft framework, open for comment through Sept. 30, that would let issuers and merchants verify whether an AI agent's purchase falls within the spending limits and duration a consumer actually authorized. The proposed "Intent Services" layer would track mandates across recurring and cumulative transactions rather than relying on a single valid card credential.
articles.tieback: As agentic payments infrastructure catches up on authorization and intent tracking, the harder bottleneck for suppliers stays upstream: getting accurate order, inventory and pricing data into the transaction in the first place, which is where Logicbroker's automated EDI and intelligent routing already do the work.

articles.title: The perfect mix: How convenience stores can balance human ideas and AI in SKU planning
articles.author: Michael Brady
articles.summary: Convenience store operators are using AI tools to spot sales patterns and flag assortment gaps, but experts from Bain, Accenture, BCG and LatentView note the technology only works once it is connected to existing POS and financial systems, and the final call on adding or cutting a SKU still belongs to a human merchant. Assortment redesign paired with the right technology typically drives a 1% to 3% sales increase and a 2% to 5% margin improvement.
articles.tieback: The article's core warning, that AI recommendations are worthless if the underlying system data isn't integrated and trustworthy, is the same problem Logicbroker's supplier analytics and SKU onboarding speed solve at the vendor connection layer before any AI ever sees the data.

articles.title: Retailers bet on AI for supply chain, 'smart' shopping
articles.author: Paige Gross
articles.summary: Executives from Gap, Dollar General, Ulta Beauty and Kohl's used their Q2 earnings calls to detail AI investments in supply chain, personalization and internal workflows, with Dollar General describing plans to build "agentic operating systems" for enterprise-wide processes and Ulta citing AI-powered sourcing to optimize omnichannel inventory.
articles.tieback: Retailers building agentic systems for inventory and sourcing need trading partner data flowing in real time to act on, the same requirement Logicbroker's real-time order and inventory visibility and automated EDI were built to satisfy for supplier networks.

articles.title: The AI Industry Is Now Selling Decisions
articles.author: Tiffany Chang
articles.summary: Chang argues enterprises are shifting from paying for AI model access to paying per decision, since routine tasks like summarizing or classifying don't need frontier-level intelligence while complex reasoning does. She compares it to routing electricity, where not every device needs the same power, and predicts companies will increasingly measure AI by the value created per interaction rather than by leaderboard rank.
articles.tieback: This right-size-the-intelligence-for-the-task logic maps directly onto supply chain automation, where high-volume, structured decisions like PO matching, inventory sync and routing don't need a human or a frontier model in the loop, the exact work Logicbroker's automated EDI and intelligent routing already handle.

articles.title: Spreedly Sees Good Bots Becoming an Agentic Commerce Channel
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Spreedly's Adam Hiatt tells PYMNTS that AI-driven bot traffic is shifting from a fraud risk to a revenue channel, with one ticketing customer seeing LLM-originated sessions convert at two to three times the rate of search traffic. He argues merchants now need to treat catalog accuracy and machine-readable product data as commercial infrastructure, since agents largely decide before they ever reach a merchant's site.
articles.tieback: Catalog accuracy and machine-readable inventory data are becoming the entry ticket for agent-driven sales, which is exactly the real-time inventory visibility and SKU onboarding speed Logicbroker gives retailers and suppliers today.

articles.title: How 23% of Merchants Captured Retail's Next Agentic Commerce Advantage
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: A new PYMNTS Intelligence/Visa Acceptance Solutions study finds only 23% of merchants can clearly identify both AI-driven traffic and purchases today, even though 61% expect AI results to influence purchases more than traditional search and 56% expect agents to complete transactions outright. The report frames attribution, not the smartest shopping agent, as the first real competitive advantage in agentic commerce.
articles.tieback: Most merchants lack the order and transaction visibility to even see agent-driven demand, a gap Logicbroker's real-time order and inventory visibility is built to close before competitors figure out attribution.

articles.title: H&M Tracks Store Inventory in Real Time With RFID, AI
articles.author: Dan Berthiaume
articles.summary: H&M Group is rolling out GreyOrange's AI-based gStore platform, which pairs RFID readers and smart mirrors to locate inventory within three to five feet and flag which SKUs sell fastest or get abandoned in fitting rooms. The retailer is layering this on top of an existing GreyOrange warehouse robotics deployment to speed replenishment and picking across hundreds of stores.
articles.tieback: H&M is paying for real-time, SKU-level inventory visibility to fix replenishment gaps, the same problem Logicbroker's real-time order and inventory visibility solves at the vendor and dropship level before product ever reaches a store.

articles.title: Dollar General Deploys AI Across Distribution Centers, Stores
articles.author: Kelly Stroh
articles.summary: Dollar General is using Relex Solutions' AI platform to unify forecasting, replenishment and allocation across its 21,000 stores and 34 distribution centers, folding ordering schedules, lead times and supplier coordination into one system. CEO Todd Vasos said the company is also building "agentic operating systems" to reshape workflows enterprise-wide.
articles.tieback: Unifying supplier coordination and fulfillment data into one planning layer is the same problem Logicbroker's intelligent routing and supplier analytics solve for retailers managing dropship and 3P vendor networks.

articles.title: From Inflation To AI: How Retailers Can Stay Ahead This Holiday Season
articles.author: Jill Standish (Accenture, Global Retail Lead)
articles.summary: Accenture's Jill Standish writes that retail leaders face a widening gap between AI ambition and results heading into the holidays: 56% are confident agentic AI will deliver quantifiable outcomes within 12 months, but only 17% say they've achieved widespread, sustained business value so far. She also cites Accenture research finding 74% of consumers would trust a personal AI agent more than their best friend to make a purchase on their behalf.
articles.tieback: With consumer trust in AI agents already ahead of retailer readiness, the operational bottleneck is proven infrastructure, not more pilots, which is where Logicbroker's rapid vendor onboarding and automated EDI already deliver measurable results.

articles.title: Retailers Steer AI Traffic Back to Own Checkouts
articles.author: Staff
articles.summary: Retailers including Ulta Beauty, Etsy, and The Knot are marketing products through AI platforms like Gemini and ChatGPT while working to keep the actual transaction, and the customer data that comes with it, on their own sites. A new PYMNTS Intelligence report found 49.6 million U.S. adults now begin retail product searches with AI, making the handoff between AI-driven discovery and merchant checkout a growing strategic question.
articles.tieback: As AI-driven discovery routes shoppers away from a single storefront, suppliers need real-time order and inventory visibility and fast SKU onboarding so they stay listed and fulfillable no matter which AI surface a shopper lands on next.

articles.title: Albertsons AI Assistants Drive Immediate 26% Basket Growth Among Early Adopters
articles.author: Staff (citing The Wall Street Journal)
articles.summary: Albertsons found that shoppers using its more comprehensive AI assistant, which builds recipes and shopping lists around dietary preferences, increase order value by 26%, compared to 10% for simple conversational search. The grocer is consolidating several AI tools into one assistant and is applying AI to merchandising, staffing, and supply chain optimization as well.
articles.tieback: The basket-growth lift depends on stitching product data, availability, and personalization together in real time, the same real-time order and inventory visibility that lets an AI assistant confidently promise, and actually fulfill, what it recommends.

articles.title: Batteries Plus launches AI tools for franchising, store customer service
articles.author: Dan Berthiaume
articles.summary: Batteries Plus is rolling out three AI tools: Savannah for franchise development calls, Edison for store customer service, and Wattson for AI-assisted product search, built on several years of backend modernization across e-commerce, POS, product information management, and partner integrations. The retailer says the goal is faster, more confident decisions for both corporate staff and store associates.
articles.tieback: Wattson's product-search AI only works because the underlying product data and integrations were normalized first, a reminder that automated, structured supplier data from rapid EDI and SKU onboarding is the prerequisite for any customer-facing AI tool to perform well.

articles.title: Intel report shows gap between robotics expectations and readiness
articles.author: Nathan Owens
articles.summary: A survey of 800 leaders commissioned by Intel found 70% of manufacturing and retail leaders expect to manage a fleet of robots within five years, but only about four in ten have a formal strategy for a mixed human-robot workforce. Retail scored better than smart cities and defense on readiness but still showed a meaningful gap tied to unclear ownership and workforce training.
articles.tieback: The gap between deploying automation and having the operating model to run it mirrors supplier onboarding: buying a tool doesn't fix throughput unless intelligent routing and supplier analytics are in place to actually operationalize it.

articles.title: Beyond The Hype: Agentic AI Has The Potential To Redefine Retail
articles.author: Shariq Rehman
articles.summary: Rehman argues retail's AI conversation has focused on how many tools get deployed rather than whether AI actually removes operational friction. He points to agents that trigger inventory replenishment ahead of stockouts and coordinate promotions with fulfillment capacity as the more durable use case than simple copilots.
articles.tieback: That's exactly the lever intelligent routing and supplier analytics are built for: connecting demand signals to replenishment and fulfillment decisions automatically instead of leaving them siloed across systems.

articles.title: Lowe's AI Assistant Turns Questions Into Sales
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Lowe's AI assistant Mylow has fielded more than 25 million questions since launch, and online shoppers who use it convert at three times the rate of those who don't, CEO Marvin Ellison said on the retailer's Q2 earnings call. Home Depot's comparable tool, Magic Apron, follows the same model, turning a vague project question into a specific, purchasable list of products rather than a set of search results.
articles.tieback: Both tools show agents winning by translating unstructured shopper intent directly into a purchasable basket, the same kind of structured, transaction-ready product data that depends on clean SKU and catalog onboarding to work at scale.

articles.title: Microsoft Puts 25 AI Agents to Work on Supply Chain Costs
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Microsoft has deployed more than 25 AI agents across its own supply chain to simulate demand, flag freight billing discrepancies, and recommend shipping routes, building on an Azure data lake it began consolidating in 2018. A related deployment at Dow uses agents to catch invoice errors across roughly 4,000 daily shipments, recovering millions in freight overpayments.
articles.tieback: The freight-auditing use case, matching invoices against contracts and shipment history at scale, is the same discrepancy-catching problem automated EDI and real-time order visibility are built to solve for drop-ship and 3P networks.

articles.title: Why Merchants Save Their Best Offers for Checkout
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: A PYMNTS Intelligence and FIS study of 60 grocery, retail and restaurant merchants finds only 27% can currently deliver one-to-one offers in real time, even though most describe their underlying data as advanced. Checkout-integrated promotions are already merchants' most-used and best-performing promotional channel, and 25% plan to prioritize real-time checkout optimization in future budgets.
articles.tieback: The gap merchants describe, having the data but not the real-time system to act on it inside a transaction, is exactly what real-time order and inventory visibility is meant to close.

articles.title: From Visibility To Action: Implementing AI For Better Retail Execution
articles.author: Brett Beveridge
articles.summary: The piece argues retailers are investing heavily in AI-powered computer vision and image recognition to verify store execution, but that value only materializes when the technology is paired with strong operational processes, clean data and clear accountability for acting on what it finds. Visibility without a defined owner and response process just produces more dashboards, not better outcomes.
articles.tieback: The argument, that AI insight is worthless without clean underlying data and a defined process to act on it, applies just as directly to catalog, inventory and order data across a supplier network as it does to in-store execution.

articles.title: The Questions Retail Leaders Should Ask Before Investing In AI
articles.author: Melissa Wong
articles.summary: With 97% of retail organizations planning to increase AI spending, the piece argues AI tools are only as reliable as the underlying data and systems feeding them, and lays out questions retailers should ask vendors about data lineage, integration and accuracy during discovery calls. It frames AI evaluation as a data-readiness exercise first, a tool-selection exercise second.
articles.tieback: The vendor-vetting questions the piece recommends, on data lineage and system integration, are the same diligence retailers should apply to supplier onboarding and EDI connections before layering AI on top of them.

articles.title: Ecommerce Trends: What's different about Amazon's approach to AI commerce
articles.summary: Digital Commerce 360's latest AI Commerce Rankings show Amazon barely cracking the top 100, because it channels shoppers into its own AI ecosystem (Rufus, Alexa) rather than optimizing for third-party AI referral traffic the way Walmart and Target do. Smaller, less-known retailers are picking up outsized traffic share from ChatGPT and Gemini precisely because they don't have a proprietary assistant competing for that same attention.
articles.tieback: Retailers without a dominant first-party AI assistant need a transactionable presence across every LLM and agent surface, not just one, which is the exact gap a structured, real-time product feed closes for suppliers who want to be discoverable and purchasable regardless of which agent the shopper is using.

articles.title: Draco Diamond credits AEO, AI traffic trends ahead of Cyber 5
articles.summary: Jewelry brand Draco Diamond saw a 31x jump in traffic after investing in answer engine optimization, with AI referral share climbing from 0.18% to 5.45% and those visitors spending 20% longer on-site. The catch: as a made-to-order brand, it still runs a 14-to-21-day fulfillment window, which its founder calls painful for customers who just spent significant money.
articles.tieback: Winning AI referral traffic is wasted if fulfillment can't keep pace with it, which is why automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility matter as much as AI discoverability once an agent-driven sale actually closes.

articles.title: Dollar General unifies inventory forecasting, replenishment with AI
articles.author: Zachary Russell
articles.summary: Dollar General is partnering with Relex Solutions to unify forecasting, replenishment, and allocation across its 21,000-plus stores and 34 distribution centers, spanning roughly 18,000 SKUs. The platform will also manage ordering schedules, lead times, and supplier coordination in one system so stores and distribution centers work from the same data.
articles.tieback: This is the same fragmented, high-SKU-count problem that intelligent routing and supplier analytics are built to solve for retailers running dropship or 3P programs where inventory sits with vendors instead of in owned distribution centers.

articles.title: The Real Future Of Supply Chain AI Involves Decision Orchestration
articles.author: Nirmal Jingar
articles.summary: The piece argues that as supply chains hand more decisions to AI, the hard problem shifts from model accuracy to governance: explainability, privacy, security, fairness, and measurable value all need stronger rules before autonomous decision-making can be trusted at scale.
articles.tieback: As agentic decision-making spreads into supplier and inventory workflows, auditability of every automated transaction becomes a real differentiator rather than a compliance afterthought.

articles.title: Why The Next Trillion-Dollar Opportunity Is AI-Powered Experiences
articles.author: Mirjana Perkovic
articles.summary: Perkovic argues the next wave of valuable companies won't win by having AI, but by using it to make ordinary experiences memorable, pointing to world models and embodied AI/service robots reshaping retail, travel, and logistics.
articles.tieback: The operational layer behind the experience is what makes or breaks it, and that puts a premium on the unglamorous fundamentals (fast vendor onboarding, clean product data, reliable order flow) that let a retailer actually deliver on an AI-driven promise.

articles.title: Study Finds Consumers Ready to Use AI for Holiday Shopping: Retailers Aren't
articles.author: Marianne Wilson
articles.summary: Narvar's 2026 Holiday Shopping Report finds 65% of consumers plan to use AI for at least part of their holiday shopping, from gift discovery to post-purchase tracking, but only 8% of retailers describe themselves as very confident using AI to improve the shopping experience. Most shoppers say they'll trade delivery speed for free shipping, but a meaningful share still expects free shipping to also mean fast.
articles.tieback: Retailers behind on AI readiness will need real-time order and inventory visibility to actually deliver on the speed and accuracy that AI-informed shoppers now expect.

articles.title: Synchrony Says AI Has Put Every Checkout in Play
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: Synchrony's Maran Nalluswami says agentic commerce is forcing payments and retail companies to make investment decisions before they know where a transaction will actually close, since AI platforms could become the point of purchase rather than just a research stop. Large retailers are already pushing to have products and payment options available wherever a consumer's AI agent shops, while smaller merchants just want the experience kept simple.
articles.tieback: As AI platforms move from research tool to transaction point, retailers need a transactable presence on those platforms, meaning clean, current, agent-readable catalog and inventory data ready to sell through.

articles.title: Retailers Are Making Delivery Promises Their Networks Can't Keep
articles.author: Nishith Rastogi
articles.summary: Marketing and e-commerce teams often set delivery dates without input from the people managing warehouse and carrier capacity, a gap that widens further once peak-season order volume spikes. The author argues real-time operational visibility, not just faster shipping, is what lets retailers set delivery promises their networks can actually hit.
articles.tieback: Real-time order and inventory visibility is exactly the fix here: a checkout date is only as reliable as the fulfillment and supplier data feeding it.

articles.title: AI Won't Fix a Store That Was Never Built to Run It
articles.author: Tim McCracken
articles.summary: A 2026 Deloitte survey found 75% of retail and CPG executives call AI a top strategic priority, but only 16.5% can quantify a return, largely because spend goes toward underlying infrastructure instead of the use cases it's meant to support. The author argues retailers need to assess their network as a whole system before layering on each new AI application, or risk compounding technical debt.
articles.tieback: The same logic applies further upstream: piling AI on top of a brittle, manually patched vendor integration layer just compounds the same debt, which is why automated EDI and fast vendor onboarding need to be the foundation before AI gets added on top.

articles.title: Generative AI in E-Commerce: Where the Returns Come From and How to Capture Them
articles.author: Dennis Vorobyov
articles.summary: The author cites data showing companies that deploy generative AI well see an average $3.70 return per $1 invested, yet only about 5% of companies are "future-built" enough to capture that value, starting with clean, current, well-structured product data since AI systems can only recommend what they can read. Winners like Klarna and Stitch Fix pair AI with human judgment rather than fully automating, and purchased AI solutions succeed roughly twice as often as in-house builds according to MIT research.
articles.tieback: "AI can only recommend what it can read" is the practical case for fast, clean SKU onboarding and structured catalog data as the foundation any agentic or generative shopping experience depends on.

articles.title: Instacart's AI Assistant Turns Chitchat Into Cha-Ching
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: Instacart is extending its retail media business into Cart Assistant, its AI shopping tool built on 1.6 billion lifetime orders, and is testing three new ad formats designed for conversational shopping. The rollout follows Instacart's integration with Google's Gemini and sits inside a broader race among Google, Amazon, and other platforms to own the AI-driven path from conversation to purchase.
articles.tieback: Instacart's bet shows that winning inside an AI shopping conversation depends on having a transactable, structured presence the agent can act on, the same agent-ready foundation Logicbroker builds for its retailer and supplier network.

articles.title: Malachyte Turns Spotify's Skip Signal Into a Merchant's Agentic Edge
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: Malachyte CEO Sidd Motwani describes how behavioral intelligence infrastructure built at Spotify is being applied to retail, reading a shopper's real-time actions to personalize a storefront in under 200 milliseconds. He argues agentic commerce raises the stakes because an AI agent's "consideration set" becomes the new front door, meaning a merchant can lose a sale if its product never makes an agent's shortlist.
articles.tieback: The piece underscores why real-time, machine-readable inventory and product data determine whether an AI agent even considers a merchant's catalog, which is the order and inventory visibility problem Logicbroker's platform solves for dropship and 3P suppliers.

articles.title: Lowe's Online Sales Benefit From Mylow AI Agent's Conversion Rate in Q2 2026
articles.author: Abbas Haleem
articles.summary: Lowe's reported online sales growth of 15.7% in fiscal Q2 2026, nearly twice its total sales growth, with CEO Marvin Ellison crediting its Mylow AI shopping agent alongside expanded fulfillment options. The company said the conversion rate for customers who use Mylow is triple that of customers who do not, after the tool fielded more than 25 million questions since launch.
articles.tieback: Mylow's conversion lift is a direct payoff of clean, structured product data at scale, the same catalog foundation Logicbroker's rapid SKU onboarding gives dropship and 3P vendors before an AI assistant can act on their listings.

articles.title: 3M Uses AI to Tame Its 60,000-Product Portfolio
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: 3M launched Ask 3M, an AI assistant that answers technical product questions in plain language, grounded in the company's own documentation across 49 technology platforms rather than open internet data. The company paired it with a Digital Materials Hub that lets engineers test materials virtually, aiming to shorten the path from research to purchase across a 60,000-SKU catalog.
articles.tieback: 3M's problem, a massive catalog where incomplete or siloed product data costs sales, is the same one Logicbroker's automated EDI and SKU onboarding speed solve for retailers trying to make thousands of supplier catalogs usable and searchable.

articles.title: Algorithmic Shopping Is Here. Is Your Company Ready?
articles.author: Paul F. Accornero
articles.summary: Accornero traces how Amazon's Buy for Me, OpenAI's Instant Checkout, Google's Universal Commerce Protocol, and Microsoft's Copilot Checkout have each pushed AI agents further into the purchase decision, not just product discovery. He argues executives who spent years preparing their organizations to use AI internally now face a harder challenge: preparing for AI as the customer.
articles.tieback: The piece frames the same shift Logicbroker is built for. Treating AI agents as a real buying channel means retailers and suppliers need a transactable presence on LLMs and agents, not just a human-facing storefront.

articles.title: No Discount Survives an AI That Can't See It
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: Synchrony's August 17 enterprise deal with OpenAI will let shoppers browse promotional financing and partner offers inside ChatGPT, following Target's setup where Circle discounts already apply automatically once a shopper connects their account inside Microsoft Copilot or Google's AI surfaces. The piece argues a loyalty benefit an AI agent cannot read effectively doesn't exist for purposes of a purchase decision, since the agent can only weigh what's exposed to it.
articles.tieback: A supplier's promotions, pricing, and terms only influence an AI-mediated purchase if they're exposed through structured, machine-readable data, which is exactly what automated EDI and real-time catalog feeds are built to guarantee.

articles.title: How Payment Leaders Can Win Agentic Commerce
articles.author: Lital Marom
articles.summary: Marom cites survey data showing about 65% of shoppers trust AI to compare prices while only 14% trust it to place an order, and argues the gap closes through control rather than more autonomy: spending caps, instant revocation, and easy cancellation that let an agent earn a purchase instead of assuming it. She frames judgment and discernment, not raw automation, as the scarce asset payment and commerce leaders need to supply.
articles.tieback: The same trust gap applies to supplier-facing automation. Retailers only let a routing engine or buying agent commit to an order when the supplier analytics and intelligent routing behind it give a clear, auditable basis for the decision.

articles.title: Amazon Envisions Next-Generation Automated Stations to Process Packages 2.5 Times Faster
articles.author: PYMNTS Staff
articles.summary: Amazon is developing an automated delivery-station concept, internally called Project Tetromino, that would use AI and robotics to organize packages and prep them for delivery vehicles at roughly 2.5 times the throughput of its current stations, with a pilot facility targeted for 2028. Amazon disputed the leaked timeline and financial projections but confirmed the project is real and still early-stage.
articles.tieback: As AI-driven sortation compresses fulfillment speed on the outbound side, the bottleneck shifts upstream to how fast a supplier's inventory and order data can feed that automation, the same problem intelligent routing and real-time inventory visibility solve on the vendor side.

articles.title: Target highlights in-stock gains as turnaround plan advances
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: Target COO Lisa Roath said the retailer hit its strongest item availability in recent years for its most frequently purchased products, crediting closer coordination between supply chain, merchandising and store teams plus prepositioned inventory and dedicated trailer capacity ahead of back-to-school. Target is also using Proxima, a digital twin of its middle-mile inventory system announced August 13, to simulate supply chain decisions before executing them.
articles.tieback: Proxima is a simulation layer bolted onto existing inventory flows after the fact. A platform with real-time order and inventory visibility built in from the start gives suppliers and retailers that same downstream-impact clarity without a separate digital-twin project.

articles.title: FIS Says Purchase Data Will Push Payments Beyond the Transaction
articles.author: Jakob Harrison (FIS)
articles.summary: FIS senior vice president Jakob Harrison argues payments executives should treat AI and agentic commerce as an accumulation of smaller signals rather than one defining event, and describes FIS's Smart Basket strategy as a bet that item-level purchase data, not just the fact a payment occurred, is what makes a transaction useful to an AI agent. He calls the shift a move from transaction processing to transaction intelligence.
articles.tieback: An AI agent, or any automated buying system, is only as useful as the item-level data behind the transaction, the same argument for why SKU onboarding speed and real-time order data matter more than payment processing alone in a dropship or 3P network.

articles.title: AI Agents Could Rewrite E-Commerce—Here's How Brands Can Prepare
articles.author: Haozhuang Dai
articles.summary: AI shopping agents collapse discovery, evaluation and checkout into a single conversation, which means brands lose the traditional multi-step funnel where content, ads and product listings functioned as separate disciplines. Dai argues large language models don't experience brands the way people do, so retailers need structured, machine-readable product data to get recommended in an agent's shortlist.
articles.tieback: Brands whose catalog data isn't structured and machine-readable risk disappearing from agent shortlists entirely, which is exactly the gap Logicbroker's transactionable presence on LLMs and agents and standardized SKU onboarding are built to close.

articles.title: Amazon, Fulfillment Tech Company AutoStore Ink Global Supply Deal
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: AutoStore agreed to a framework for Amazon to further procure its automated storage and retrieval systems worldwide, though the deal includes no purchase commitments yet. The pact adds an outside automation partner to Amazon's already heavy in-house investment in robotic arms and warehouse automation, and a supply chain consultant called it a wake-up call for Target, Walmart and Kroger to move faster on their own automation.
articles.tieback: As automation raises the bar for fulfillment speed at Amazon's scale, mid-market retailers need supplier-side intelligent routing and analytics, not warehouse robotics budgets, to keep pace on delivery promises.

articles.title: Home Depot Rolls Out Express Delivery in 3 Hours or Less Across US
articles.author: Kelly Stroh
articles.summary: Home Depot launched nationwide express delivery promising eligible orders in three hours or less, using its supply chain network and more than 2,000 U.S. stores as fulfillment hubs for a flat $7 to $10 fee covering thousands of SKUs. The retailer said it has cut U.S. delivery lead times 45% over the last 18 months as part of a broader push to speed up its distribution network.
articles.tieback: Turning thousands of stores into fulfillment nodes only works with accurate, real-time SKU-level inventory across every location, the same visibility problem Logicbroker's real-time order and inventory visibility solves for dropship and 3P networks.

articles.title: Amazon to Expand Drone Delivery Reach Sixfold This Year
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: Amazon is expanding Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026, a sixfold increase, adding metro areas including Atlanta, Chicago and Cleveland. Drone delivery now covers roughly 60% of Amazon's most frequently purchased items and competes directly with Walmart's drone partnership with Wing and DoorDash's new in-house drone program.
articles.tieback: As delivery speed becomes a competitive front well beyond Amazon and Walmart's scale, smaller retailers and suppliers need intelligent order routing that picks the fastest fulfillment path from existing inventory rather than building drone infrastructure of their own.

articles.title: The Real E-Commerce AI Revolution (And Why It's Not About Efficiency)
articles.author: David Greenblatt
articles.summary: Greenblatt argues the first wave of AI for online selling just executed tasks faster (writing, optimizing, summarizing), while the bigger unclaimed opportunity is using AI to improve decision quality itself, citing Q4 inventory investment as an example where AI should weigh demand, sell-through and ad spend together instead of producing a plain statistical forecast. He extends the same logic to seller financial planning, arguing sellers need to understand margin, cash tied up in inventory and the true cost of growth.
articles.tieback: Better inventory decisions depend on having real-time order and inventory data to feed the model in the first place, which is the visibility gap Logicbroker's real-time order and inventory visibility is built to close for dropship and 3P sellers.

articles.title: AIibaba Focuses on Agentic Commerce as AI Spending Balloons
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Alibaba's Q2 earnings showed AI investment driving a 75% drop in net income even as cloud and AI-product revenue surged, with CEO Eddie Wu detailing plans for Qwen-based AI agents built specifically for eCommerce, spanning shopper-facing search and merchant operations alike. More than 250 million users have already completed a first AI-driven shopping experience through Alibaba's Qwen model.
articles.tieback: As Alibaba builds agents that plug directly into merchant data for pricing, marketing and customer service, retailers running on manual vendor onboarding and fragmented catalog feeds will struggle to keep pace with suppliers whose data is already agent-ready.

articles.title: Ecommerce Trends: Which online retailers AI is helping the most
articles.summary: Digital Commerce 360's AI Commerce Rankings show the retailers benefiting most from AI-driven traffic aren't necessarily the largest ones: niche players like Nixon, Online Labels and CustomInk climbed fastest, while categories like automotive parts gained an average of 20 positions and flowers and gifts fell nearly 18. The rankings suggest AI shopping agents reward well-structured product data over sheer scale.
articles.tieback: Category-level winners and losers in AI-referred traffic show that catalog structure and product data quality, not company size, determine which retailers get surfaced to AI shopping agents, the same fast, accurate SKU onboarding Logicbroker builds for.

articles.title: Retailers Report AI-Driven Sales and Bigger Baskets in Q2 Earnings
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Walmart, Amazon and Target all told Q2 earnings calls that AI shopping assistants are driving bigger orders (Walmart's Sparky and Amazon's Alexa for Shopping users each spend roughly 40% more per order), but nearly all the hard numbers so far come from grocery and other repeat-purchase categories. Discovery-driven retailers like TJX and Etsy show AI adoption lagging well behind in categories built on browsing rather than repetition.
articles.tieback: The gap between AI's grocery success and its weak showing in discovery categories comes down to whether the underlying product and SKU data is clean and structured enough for an assistant to act on it, exactly the gap real-time catalog and inventory visibility is built to close.

articles.title: Shoppers are finally telling grocers why they buy
articles.author: Daniel Vitiello
articles.summary: Conversational AI shopping means customers now describe their full situation, budget and constraints upfront instead of typing keywords, and Cooklist's Daniel Vitiello argues grocers need machine-readable product metadata (allergens, prep time, dietary fit) to act on that declared intent. He also argues grocers should shift from item-by-item lists toward personalized bundles assembled from a shopper's stated needs.
articles.tieback: This is a direct case for SKU-level metadata depth and structured catalog data, the same foundation that determines whether a retailer's suppliers can be onboarded and represented accurately enough for AI agents to shop from.

articles.title: The Questions Retail Leaders Should Ask Before Investing In AI
articles.author: Melissa Wong
articles.summary: Wong argues AI investments only pay off when the data and systems feeding them are sound, and lays out questions retail leaders should ask vendors about data provenance, system integration and workflow fit before signing on. She frames most AI failures as data and process failures rather than model failures.
articles.tieback: Her framework for vetting AI vendors on data quality and integration readiness is the same diligence a retailer should apply before trusting a supplier network's EDI and catalog feeds to power automated operations.

articles.title: Target Touts Jump in Traffic From AI Platforms as Sales Climb
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Target's Q2 2026 earnings call credited agentic commerce partnerships with OpenAI and other AI platforms for digital traffic growing more than 3.5 times faster than the industry average. CEO Michael Fiddelke also pointed to Proxima, a digital twin of Target's middle-mile supply chain, as key to making faster inventory decisions between buildings and stores.
articles.tieback: Target's Proxima digital twin is the kind of real-time order and inventory visibility retailers need before they can safely expose products to AI-agent traffic, since AI-referred shoppers who hit a stockout won't come back through that channel.

articles.title: Adobe: AI E-Commerce Traffic Booms, but Many Retailers Lag Behind
articles.summary: Adobe found AI-referred traffic to U.S. retail sites up 62% year over year in July, converting 60% better than non-AI traffic, but homepage visibility for AI shopping agents has actually dropped to an average of 61% across a broader set of retail sites, meaning nearly 40% of content isn't fully readable by shopping agents. Readability varies widely by vertical, from 76% in apparel down to 59% in grocery.
articles.tieback: A retailer's product catalog is only as transactable as its underlying data is machine-readable, which is the same clean, structured SKU and attribute data that makes for fast supplier onboarding and a real transactable presence on LLMs and agents.

articles.title: Regional Convenience Retailer Weigel's Unifies Store Operations at POS
articles.summary: Weigel's is rolling out Tote's AI-native POS platform across all 90 of its Tennessee convenience stores, combining point of sale, back office, foodservice, and store operations into a single cloud-based system. The retailer says the goal is to simplify operations and make it easier to adopt new store technology as it emerges.
articles.tieback: Collapsing fragmented back-office systems into one connected platform is the same problem automated EDI and real-time order visibility solve on the supplier side, replacing a patchwork of disconnected data feeds with one operational source of truth.

articles.title: How DTC Startups Are Using AI to Scale More Efficiently
articles.author: Gabriela Barkho
articles.summary: Founders from brands including Murphy Door and Vaila Shoes described using AI to price custom orders in real time and manage wholesale relationships with partners like Macy's, DSW, and Home Depot without adding headcount. Murphy Door's CEO said AI-assisted pricing now turns a product roughly every six minutes while costs trend down rather than up.
articles.tieback: These are lean teams using automation to do the pricing and partner-management work that used to require a bigger back office, the same efficiency gain suppliers get from rapid vendor onboarding and intelligent routing instead of manually managing each retail partner's requirements.

articles.title: As Lululemon AI Chief Exits, Analysts 'Increasingly Concerned' About Turnover
articles.author: Cara Salpini
articles.summary: Lululemon's chief AI and technology officer departed after less than a year, alongside a separate chief strategy officer exit, just a month before incoming CEO Heidi O'Neill starts. Analysts at BNP Paribas flagged the back-to-back C-suite departures as a talent-retention risk heading into a leadership transition.
articles.tieback: When AI strategy lives inside one executive's head instead of a stable platform, retailers lose momentum every time that person leaves, which is the argument for durable, vendor-agnostic infrastructure like EDI and onboarding automation that survives leadership changes.

articles.title: Visa and Mastercard Join Rain's Agentic Commerce Coalition
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Stablecoin infrastructure company Rain launched the Agentic Payments Alliance on Aug. 18, with Visa, Mastercard, Fiserv, Circle, Solana and Remitly among more than 25 founding members. The coalition plans to develop shared standards for how AI agents get authorized to transact, how fraud gets caught, and how loyalty and rewards travel with an agent, ahead of McKinsey's projected $3 trillion to $5 trillion agentic commerce market by 2030.
articles.tieback: A multi-network coalition is now writing the rules for how agents get authorized to transact, which raises the bar for suppliers whose EDI and order data aren't clean enough to meet those same machine-readable standards.

articles.title: What Consumers Will Actually Let AI Buy For Them
articles.author: Michael Quoc
articles.summary: Quoc argues consumer trust in AI purchasing follows an "autonomy curve" that declines as price rises and never flattens, since shoppers verify recommendations once real money is at stake. He cites Gartner data showing no more than 11% of shoppers will let AI complete a purchase on its own even in low-stakes categories like household supplies, despite McKinsey's multitrillion-dollar agentic commerce forecast.
articles.tieback: If shoppers verify before an agent completes a purchase, the product and inventory data an agent shows at that moment (accurate stock, pricing, delivery windows) becomes the deciding factor, which is exactly what real-time order and inventory visibility is built to guarantee.

articles.title: Schnucks beefs up its digital tools for shoppers
articles.author: Catherine Douglas Moran
articles.summary: Schnuck Markets added an AI shopping assistant, built with VitalityIP on more than 6 billion lines of shopping, health and nutrition data, plus a fully interactive weekly ad that lets shoppers clip coupons and build carts directly from sale listings. The 112-store grocer said the tools are meant to deepen customer relationships around nutrition, budget and meal planning.
articles.tieback: An AI assistant that recommends products from weekly deals is only as good as the underlying catalog and promotion data feeding it, the same SKU-level accuracy problem rapid vendor onboarding and automated EDI are built to solve at scale.

articles.title: 3 ways Kimberly-Clark is using technology to boost supply chain efficiency
articles.author: Phil Neuffer
articles.summary: Kimberly-Clark finished rolling out a unified Coupa procurement platform to 90% of its suppliers and began scaling an AI manufacturing agent that delivered a 40% to 50% productivity gain on knowledge-search tasks, part of a five-year, $3 billion productivity program. The company also launched an internal "IT Digital University" to train supply chain staff on AI and data visualization.
articles.tieback: A single supplier-facing platform is what made Kimberly-Clark's AI agent useful in the first place, the same argument for consolidating supplier onboarding and analytics onto one platform rather than layering AI on top of fragmented systems.

articles.title: Why Agentic AI Could Transform Procurement
articles.author: Heiner Himmelreich, Ilan Oshri, Paolo Scala and Anas Zaidani
articles.summary: The authors argue procurement is better suited to agentic AI than most business functions because its work is structured and financially measurable, yet adoption stays low for organizational rather than technical reasons. Companies seeing gains are redesigning procurement around AI, giving procurement ownership of deployments, strengthening data foundations, and measuring commercial outcomes instead of usage.
articles.tieback: The article's core barrier, weak data foundations, is the same problem intelligent routing and supplier analytics are meant to fix before an agent can make a reliable purchasing decision.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Consumers will let AI agents perform these shopping tasks
articles.summary: A DOSS-commissioned survey of 1,000 U.S. consumers found 77% would let an AI agent shop for them in some capacity, mostly to monitor prices or compare products, but only 6% would let an agent complete a purchase entirely on its own. The survey also found roughly 10% of 500 major retailers block AI shopping crawlers via robots.txt, rising to 23% among marketplaces.
articles.tieback: The robots.txt-blocking finding is a proxy for how many retailers aren't yet structured for agent discovery, the same transactionable-presence gap Logicbroker's supplier data feeds are built to close.

articles.title: AI Agents Just Got Their Own Company Credit Cards
articles.summary: Mercury launched Agent Cards, virtual corporate cards that AI agents can use autonomously within a set budget and merchant list, with out-of-policy transactions auto-declined. Ramp is pursuing a similar model through its Visa partnership, positioning agent purchasing as a new category of cardholder inside existing spend-management systems.
articles.tieback: As agents get their own purchasing credentials, the constraint shifts to whether a supplier's catalog, pricing and order data are structured well enough for an agent to transact against, the same SKU and inventory readiness problem Logicbroker solves for dropship vendors today.

articles.title: UPS Automates 90% of Daily Customs Clearances With AI Agents
articles.summary: UPS used agentic AI to lift same-day customs clearance from 21% to 90% of packages even as daily volume needing review grew nearly ninefold after the U.S. de minimis exemption ended, running classification, documentation and error checking as one continuous workflow instead of three manual steps. UPS paired this with a digital twin of its network that refreshes every 10 minutes and expanded RFID tracking across its delivery fleet.
articles.tieback: Collapsing a three-step manual document review into one automated workflow is the same leap Logicbroker's automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility deliver for retailers managing high-volume dropship transactions with suppliers.

articles.title: Clorox says ERP transition will provide supply chain gains this year
articles.author: Antone Gonsalves
articles.summary: Clorox's CFO told investors its new ERP, now past its early rollout disruptions, is shifting the company from spreadsheet-driven planning to automated, integrated business planning that should lower inventory levels and let supply chain teams respond proactively to demand signals. The upgrade is part of a five-year, $500 million data infrastructure effort that began in 2021.
articles.tieback: Clorox needed a five-year, $500 million systems overhaul to get real-time demand visibility internally, which underscores the value of a platform like Logicbroker that gives retailers that same order and inventory visibility across suppliers without a multi-year ERP replacement.

articles.title: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI?, Flipping the Business Model
articles.author: Ben Thompson
articles.summary: Ben Thompson analyzes reports that Stripe is acquiring OpenRouter, the AI model-routing marketplace, framing it as a bet on capturing Aggregation-style leverage over the market for AI models rather than just payments. He weighs whether the deal signals Stripe shifting from a payments-take-rate business into an AI infrastructure aggregator.
articles.tieback: The same aggregation logic applies to commerce data: whoever sits at the chokepoint between retailer demand and supplier fulfillment, the role Logicbroker plays for dropship and 3P networks, captures outsized leverage as more transactions route through AI intermediaries.

articles.title: AI Is Bringing Retailers Their Best Customers but Not Closing the Sale
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Etsy and DoorDash executives say AI-referred shopping traffic converts at a higher rate and larger order size, but agentic order volume remains under 1% of total because handoffs to real inventory, fulfillment, and checkout still don't work reliably. Adobe data shows AI-referred traffic to U.S. retail sites up 393% year over year, yet PYMNTS Intelligence finds only 49% of shoppers trust an agent to actually complete a purchase.
articles.tieback: The gap these executives describe, connecting an AI agent's interest to real inventory and fulfillment data at the moment of purchase, is exactly what real-time order and inventory visibility and a transactionable presence on LLMs and agents are built to close.

articles.title: Amazon Wants Alexa to Look Inside the Fridge and Fill the Cart
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Amazon's Alexa for Shopping combines photos of a customer's fridge, conversation, and purchase history to build a household shopping list automatically, an attempt to have AI infer demand before a customer states it. Walmart is countering by making its catalog available across multiple AI assistants and leaning on its store-based inventory and fulfillment footprint.
articles.tieback: Winning this race depends on a retailer's catalog and inventory data being clean and current enough for an AI agent to act on instantly, the same real-time inventory visibility and SKU onboarding speed problem dropship retailers face at scale.

articles.title: FedEx, Amazon pursue expanded use of robotic arms
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: FedEx deployed Dexterity's dual-armed Mech trailer loading robots at its Hagerstown hub and plans to expand automated loading across more than 20 U.S. hubs, while Amazon plans to more than double its robotic arms fleet in 2026. Both moves reflect an industry-wide push to automate physically demanding warehouse tasks with AI-guided robotics.
articles.tieback: Physical automation like this only pays off when the order and inventory data feeding it is accurate in real time, which is why intelligent routing and supplier analytics matter as much as the robots themselves.

articles.title: Walmart equipping a store with Symbotic fulfillment system
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: Symbotic has begun installing its first SymMicro back-of-store fulfillment system inside a Walmart location, using autonomous robots to retrieve totes for e-commerce pickup and delivery orders. Walmart has committed to buying 400 of the systems as part of a multiyear automation partnership.
articles.tieback: Store-level automation like this is only as fast as the order data flowing into it, the same rapid vendor onboarding and automated EDI problem that determines how quickly a retailer's dropship and 3P suppliers can plug into a fulfillment network like this one.

articles.title: Agentic Commerce Will Redefine How Brands Compete
articles.author: Brett Davis
articles.summary: Davis argues the central question in agentic commerce is what data an AI shopping agent uses to define value, since agents will favor brands with structured, verifiable product data over persuasive marketing copy. He cites Prophet research showing 54% of consumers find autonomous agents helpful, though only 14% currently trust one to place an order.
articles.tieback: This is a direct argument for having a transactionable presence on LLMs and agents, since brands whose product data isn't structured for machine consumption will simply be invisible to the agents making the purchase decision.

articles.title: Consumers warm up to agentic AI purchases
articles.author: Tatiana Walk-Morris
articles.summary: An RTB House survey of over 1,800 shoppers across the US, UK, Japan, and France found 44% now trust AI tools more than friends and family when making purchase decisions, and 42% of American millennials would let an AI agent buy items for them within a $250 budget if a seven-day return window is included. Trust drops the closer an agent gets to actually completing payment: over a third of respondents, and 44% of baby boomers, still want a human to review the transaction first.
articles.tieback: As AI agents take on more of the actual buying decision, retailers depend on suppliers whose product and inventory data is accurate and instantly queryable, the kind of real-time visibility rapid EDI onboarding provides rather than something bolted on after the fact.

articles.title: AI Just Made Retail's Long Tail Pay Off
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Shopify President Harley Finkelstein said on the company's Aug. 5 earnings call that 75% of AI-attributed purchases last quarter came from outside the platform's top 100 product categories, with that AI-referred traffic and order volume both tripling year over year. The piece argues AI search is finally letting niche products get found without a marketing budget, but only when a retailer's structured product data, fulfillment details, and trust signals are complete enough for an AI agent to match against a specific request.
articles.tieback: Every SKU in the long tail only becomes discoverable to an AI agent once it has been onboarded with complete, accurate data, which is the exact bottleneck fast SKU onboarding and automated EDI are built to remove for suppliers with large or fast-changing catalogs.

articles.title: Where USPS could benefit the most from AI
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: A USPS Office of Inspector General report found the agency already runs more than 35 active AI use cases, with the biggest untapped opportunity in dynamic route optimization that adjusts delivery paths in real time based on traffic and volume. The report cautions that scaling AI-driven routing will need labor union buy-in and competes for investment against network modernization and workforce priorities.
articles.tieback: The routing problem USPS is only beginning to tackle with AI, matching real-time conditions to delivery decisions, is the same problem intelligent order routing and supplier analytics solve today for dropship networks moving goods across dozens of suppliers.

articles.title: Target strengthens inventory management with digital twins
articles.author: Kelly Stroh
articles.summary: Target built a digital twin called Proxima that simulates how inventory decisions will play out before its teams act on them, catching problems ahead of time; a small pilot on 63 fresh food items improved on-shelf availability by 2.5%. Proxima also modeled inventory flow into Target's new Houston Receive Center with about 98% accuracy before the facility opened.
articles.tieback: Target can afford to build a custom simulation layer for inventory visibility, but most retailers get the same real-time view into supplier stock and order flow off the shelf through a platform built for it rather than an in-house engineering project.

articles.title: Beyond The Hype: Agentic AI Has The Potential To Redefine Retail
articles.author: Shariq Rehman
articles.summary: Shariq Rehman of Visionet Systems argues retail's next AI advantage will not come from adopting more models but from connecting merchandising, supply chain, fulfillment, and store operations so decisions happen with shared context, since agentic AI cannot compensate for fragmented data or disconnected systems. He points to AI agents that could trigger inventory replenishment before a stockout or coordinate a promotion with fulfillment capacity as the real prize, not the model itself.
articles.tieback: The fragmented supplier data and disconnected systems this piece flags as the real barrier to agentic AI are exactly what automated EDI and unified order and inventory visibility exist to fix before a retailer ever gets to the agentic layer.

articles.title: Google Maps adds agentic features, including food ordering and hotel bookings
articles.author: Aisha Malik
articles.summary: Google is rolling out new agentic capabilities in its "Ask Maps" AI feature, letting users order food through Square, Toast or Uber Eats, book hotels, and buy event tickets directly from natural-language queries in Google Maps. The update also adds Personal Intelligence, which pulls context from Gmail and Calendar, and gives Ask Maps persistent conversation memory, part of Google's push to turn Maps into a task-completing assistant rather than just a navigation tool.
articles.tieback: When a bellwether like Google routes agentic food orders through a restaurant's own POS system rather than taking a cut, it validates the model where retailers and suppliers need a transactionable, EDI-connected presence so AI agents can complete orders without the merchant losing the relationship or the margin.

articles.title: Safeway plugin comes to ChatGPT
articles.author: Peyton Bigora
articles.summary: Albertsons launched a Safeway plugin inside ChatGPT that lets shoppers type "@Safeway" plus a request, such as reordering a weekly list, to get relevant product suggestions, then redirects them to Safeway's site to complete checkout. It's the latest piece of Albertsons' broader AI shopping foundation, following a December agentic assistant rollout and a February OpenAI advertising pilot.
articles.tieback: The redirect-to-checkout pattern shows retailers still need their own real-time inventory and order data exposed cleanly to the LLM at the moment of discovery, the same catalog and inventory visibility Logicbroker gives suppliers so their SKUs are accurate and ready to transact wherever the shopper actually converts.

articles.title: The RealReal's AI Overhaul Helps Drive 22% GMV Growth
articles.summary: The RealReal's AI-powered intake system, Athena, now automates authentication and cataloging for close to half of all items, up from 35% a year ago, while a pricing algorithm scoring more than 100 data points per item manages markdowns without manual override. The company also onboarded two new Japanese vendors into its international dropship program this quarter, contributing to GMV growth of 22% year over year.
articles.tieback: Athena's jump from 35% to nearly half of intake automated is a direct proof point for what fast, automated SKU and vendor onboarding does to margin and speed to sell, the same lever Logicbroker pulls for dropship and 3P suppliers through automated EDI and rapid onboarding.

articles.title: Crocs launches 10-year AI transformation program
articles.summary: Crocs signed a 10-year deal with Infosys to deploy AI-first platforms across its enterprise IT and business operations, aiming to break down data silos and enable real-time, insight-driven decision-making. The partnership targets rising operating costs and inconsistent business processes as Crocs tries to respond faster to shifting consumer demand.
articles.tieback: A decade-long bet on unifying data across silos shows how much retailers will pay to fix fragmented systems, the same fragmentation Logicbroker resolves for supplier and order data through real-time order and inventory visibility instead of a multi-year IT overhaul.

articles.title: Why Consumers Are Frustrated With AI And What Retailers Can Do About It
articles.author: Sharon Edelson
articles.summary: Consumer frustration with AI is growing as shoppers tire of generic marketing, unreliable AI customer service, and low-quality "AI slop," a disillusionment that economic uncertainty is compounding into more pragmatic, risk-averse buying behavior. Gartner projects AI agents will handle 90% of B2B purchases by 2028, raising the stakes for retailers whose AI experiences currently fall short of that trust bar.
articles.tieback: If AI fatigue is pushing shoppers toward more pragmatic, reliability-driven decisions, that raises the bar for backend data accuracy, since sloppy or delayed product and inventory info is exactly what erodes trust once it surfaces through an AI assistant, the failure mode Logicbroker's real-time inventory and order visibility is built to prevent.

articles.title: DoorDash Says Agentic Traffic Is Low, but AI Gains Are Not
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: DoorDash CEO Tony Xu told investors that agentic order volume from AI shopping assistants remains low because most AI platforms are prioritizing enterprise and coding tools over physical fulfillment, even as DoorDash's own AI tools already build a grocery cart in under two minutes and automate catalog creation for new merchants. The company's new Dash Mark warehouses, where DoorDash controls inventory directly, are delivering tenfold better order accuracy than traditional grocery partnerships.
articles.tieback: That tenfold accuracy gap between DoorDash-controlled inventory and traditional grocery partnerships is the same order and inventory visibility problem automated EDI and real-time integration are built to close for retailers leaning on third-party fulfillment.

articles.title: AI Finds the Deal, Shoppers Still Make the Call
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: New PYMNTS Intelligence data from Amazon Prime Day and Walmart Deals found 21% of shoppers, and 35% of Gen Z, used an AI chatbot while shopping, mostly to compare prices and surface deals rather than to place the actual order. Amazon and Walmart still captured the transaction even as product discovery increasingly happened inside AI tools rather than on the retailers' own sites.
articles.tieback: As product discovery moves into AI assistants before the retailer ever sees the shopper, accurate, structured product and inventory data reaching those agents becomes a prerequisite for winning the sale, not an optional add-on.

articles.title: Survey: Consumers comfortable with store robots performing 'background' work
articles.summary: A Breakwater Strategy survey conducted with YouGov found 63% of U.S. adults are comfortable with robots doing stockroom work and 59% with robots cleaning aisles, but comfort drops to the mid-40s once robots stock shelves or help customers directly, and to 39% at self-checkout. Breakwater advised retailers to communicate clearly about where and how they deploy robots given that 74% of respondents worry robots will take other people's jobs.
articles.tieback: Consumer comfort with back-of-house automation is the opening for retailers to invest in the inventory accuracy behind the scenes, the same real-time visibility that has to keep supplier and fulfillment data in sync before a robot or associate ever touches the shelf.

articles.title: AI Connects B2B Firms' 3 Biggest Challenges: Goods, Contracts and Cash
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: A new PYMNTS Intelligence Enterprise AI Benchmark report finds wholesale distributors use AI across 35 of 75 tracked business tasks, more than retail or construction, with three-quarters using it for contract generation while keeping AI agents at look-up-only access rather than letting them execute orders or payments. The report argues the real opportunity is connecting supplier contracts, inventory levels and cash flow into one coordinated system rather than treating AI as a collection of separate point tools.
articles.tieback: Coordinating supplier contracts, inventory levels and cash flow as one system is the same integration problem automated EDI and supplier analytics already solve, well ahead of most wholesalers' cautious, look-up-only approach to AI agents.

articles.title: Council Post: Your E-Commerce Storefront May Look Perfect, But AI Likely Can't Read It
articles.author: Margareta Petrovic
articles.summary: Petrovic argues that most e-commerce sites are designed for human eyes, not the AI answer engines now filtering product discovery, and that brands need a clean entity layer, structured, machine-readable facts about products and policies, before they can show up in AI-generated answers. She lays out three sequential moves: open the front door to AI crawlers, fix the entity layer, then track legibility as an ongoing metric.
articles.tieback: A clean, structured entity layer is exactly what a transactionable presence on LLMs and shopping agents requires, and it depends on the same clean, real-time product and inventory data that fast SKU onboarding is supposed to guarantee in the first place.

articles.title: Cloudflare Issues AI Agents a Wallet and Identity
articles.summary: Cloudflare introduced Cloudflare Wallets and cloudflare.pay, giving AI shopping agents a verifiable identity and a programmable way to pay on behalf of the humans or companies that deployed them. The move responds to a gap PYMNTS Intelligence has tracked for months: close to half of consumers still worry about fraud, data transparency, and reversing purchases an agent made in their name.
articles.tieback: As agent identity and payment infrastructure standardizes, sellers need product, order, and inventory data structured well enough for an agent to transact against with confidence, not just for a human to browse.

articles.title: Appeals Court Overturns Ban on Perplexity AI Shopping Agents on Amazon
articles.summary: A U.S. appeals court overturned a prior ruling that had barred Perplexity's AI shopping agents from accessing Amazon, finding it was Perplexity's users, not Perplexity itself, accessing the platform. It is the first federal appeals ruling on whether AI agents acting on a user's behalf can legally access a retailer's platform, regardless of that retailer's own wishes.
articles.tieback: Retailers can no longer assume they control whether agents show up on their site; the practical question shifts to whether product, pricing, and inventory data are clean and structured enough for an agent to transact accurately once it arrives.

articles.title: HomeBase USA rolls out inventory scanning robots following pilot
articles.author: Zachary Russell
articles.summary: After a two-store pilot, home improvement retailer HomeBase USA expanded Simbe's Tally shelf-scanning robots and Store Intelligence platform to all nine of its locations. The pilot cut pricing errors by 92%, lowered controllable out-of-stocks by 58%, and shortened annual physical inventory counts from three days to under one.
articles.tieback: The gains came entirely from continuous, real-time shelf and inventory visibility, the same principle that determines whether a dropship or 3P supplier network shows accurate stock instead of stale counts.

articles.title: AI Ends the Shipping Cost Guessing Game
articles.summary: Most retailers still quote shipping costs using static assumptions (a default box size or a historical average) instead of how a specific order actually fits into a box, and dimensional-weight pricing can bill an oversized box at nearly three times an item's real weight. Wholesale marketplace Faire and AI bin-packing tools are replacing that guesswork with per-order calculations, since 48% of shoppers who abandon carts cite unexpected shipping costs as the reason.
articles.tieback: Static, rule-based shipping and routing breaks down under real order variability the same way static EDI mappings and routing rules do; the fix in both cases is real-time data over defaults.

articles.title: AI Could Squeeze Retail's Middle Even Further
articles.author: Michelle Evans
articles.summary: Retail is polarizing between large retailers with scale and data and DTC brands with direct customer relationships, and Evans argues AI-driven discovery will intensify that split by shifting competition from product access to visibility in AI recommendations. Mid-market retailers that lack both scale and first-party relationships face the sharpest exposure as passive browsing gives way to AI-mediated consideration.
articles.tieback: Mid-market retailers and their suppliers can offset scale disadvantages with speed, fast vendor and SKU onboarding and broad assortment reach, so AI discovery engines have more of their catalog to recommend from.

articles.title: AI Voice Agents Take Over the Retail Sales Floor
articles.author: PYMNTS
articles.summary: Japanese appliance retailer Yamada Denki built a 24/7 multilingual voice agent on OpenAI's GPT-Realtime that guided roughly 30,000 shoppers through purchases in a two-week campaign, asking the same probing questions a floor associate would instead of waiting for keyword prompts. PYMNTS Intelligence data cited in the piece shows 45% of consumers already say they'd let an AI agent complete a purchase on their behalf, and 43% of retailers are piloting autonomous shopping agents now.
articles.tieback: As agents move from answering questions to closing sales, they're only as good as the product and inventory data feeding them, the case a transactionable, agent-ready product feed is meant to make for a retailer's catalog.

articles.title: AI Agents Need Rules Before They Can Run Payments
articles.author: Colin Swain, Bottomline
articles.summary: Bottomline's Colin Swain argues that finance functions handing real decisions to AI agents, in areas like collections, cash application and risk management, need clear rules, defined decision rights and full audit visibility before autonomy can scale. He frames the goal as "controlled autonomy," where every agent action is traceable and aligned to financial controls rather than layered on top of processes that were never built for it.
articles.tieback: That same traceability problem shows up in dropship operations, where automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility give trading partners the auditable data trail this piece says agentic finance still lacks.

articles.title: Walmart Canada Forecasts Weather Disruptions With Proprietary AI Tool
articles.author: Chain Store Age staff
articles.summary: Walmart Canada built a "storm rerouting agent" using AI-assisted coding tools that cross-references 10-day weather forecasts against real-time highway and ferry closures, carrier data and other operational signals to flag transportation disruptions before they hit. The tool was developed in-house rather than bought from a vendor, reflecting Walmart's broader push to build proprietary AI into supply chain operations.
articles.tieback: Most retailers don't have the engineering bench to build a custom disruption tool in-house, which is exactly the gap intelligent routing and supplier analytics close by rerouting orders around a disruption without a bespoke build.

articles.title: Ecommerce Trends: How Lululemon Is Using AI
articles.author: Sara Spivey
articles.summary: Lululemon is applying AI across inventory management, supply chain and procurement to cut complexity, with the goal of shrinking its go-to-market calendar from 18-24 months down to 12-14 months. The retailer named its first chief AI and technology officer in 2025 and is also using AI to sharpen search, fit and personalization on its ecommerce site.
articles.tieback: Cutting go-to-market time by a third is largely a vendor and SKU onboarding speed problem, the exact bottleneck rapid vendor onboarding for dropship and 3P suppliers is built to remove.

articles.title: Why The Future Of Agentic AI Is One Expert, Not A Hundred Specialists
articles.author: Alex Saric, Ivalua
articles.summary: Ivalua's CMO argues that stacking a separate AI specialist agent for every procurement task (supplier onboarding, risk monitoring, contract review, and more) creates a supervision burden no one can manage, since each agent works off different data with no shared context. He cites a Sapio Research survey of 800 procurement leaders where 59% said trust in AI, not cost or capability, is the bigger barrier to progress.
articles.tieback: Supplier onboarding shows up by name as one of the procurement tasks fragmenting under agent sprawl, a point in favor of one connected platform over another point-solution agent bolted onto the pile.

articles.title: Cards Make Their Case in an Agentic World
articles.summary: Mastercard, Visa, American Express and Capital One used their Q2 2026 earnings calls to stake competing claims on agentic commerce infrastructure. Mastercard is scaling Agent Pay with more than 30 partners, Visa touted 150+ AI-powered applications plus new OpenAI and Meta partnerships, Amex leaned on its closed-loop network for fraud and data advantages, and Capital One pointed to its Discover network integration as the foundation for AI-driven underwriting.
articles.tieback: As card networks race to own the trust layer for agent-initiated purchases, the harder problem for retailers stays upstream: whether their own vendor and inventory data is clean and structured enough for an agent to transact against in the first place, which is where automated EDI and real-time inventory visibility do the actual work.

articles.title: Nine Out of Ten Firms Struggle to Manage Bot Traffic
articles.summary: A PYMNTS Intelligence report produced with Trulioo finds companies are struggling to tell malicious bots from legitimate shopping agents, with 57% of billion-dollar-revenue firms reporting bot-related incidents or losses in the past year. Fraud and false blocks tied to bot traffic cost businesses close to $100 billion annually, pushing firms toward continuous identity verification instead of one-time account checks.
articles.tieback: The same identity and permissioning problem applies directly to supplier onboarding. A retailer that can verify and onboard a new dropship vendor's data feed automatically, rather than manually vetting each one, is better positioned to extend that same rigor to agent traffic without slowing down legitimate transactions.

articles.title: Schnucks turns to agentic AI shopping assistant
articles.author: Catherine Douglas Moran
articles.summary: Schnucks is rolling out an agentic AI shopping assistant that builds carts and makes recommendations based on customers' stated health and wellness preferences, joining Albertsons and Kroger in offering this kind of tool. The assistant is meant to cut the friction of finding products that fit dietary needs across a large, fast-changing catalog.
articles.tieback: Tools like this are only as good as the underlying product data behind them, so a retailer's ability to onboard and refresh SKU-level attributes quickly across suppliers directly determines whether the assistant can actually match a dietary preference to the right item in stock.

articles.title: How supply chain leaders can avoid common AI pitfalls
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: Executives speaking at a recent industry event said the biggest risks in supply chain AI adoption are starting with bad data, scaling pilots too fast, and refusing to kill use cases that don't pay off. Experts stressed that piloting deliberately and building solid data foundations matters more than moving fast.
articles.tieback: This is the recurring lesson for any retailer trying to stand up AI-driven forecasting or routing: the data foundation, not the model, is what determines whether a pilot scales, which is exactly the gap that automated EDI and real-time order and inventory visibility are built to close.

articles.title: Delaware Proposes New Legal Framework for Autonomous Agents
articles.summary: Delaware is developing a new corporate structure, the Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC), that would let an AI agent run a company's day-to-day affairs inside a regulated sandbox overseen by the Secretary of State and Attorney General. The proposal, developed with legal AI firm Norm Ai, aims to give autonomous agents a recognized legal identity so liability and accountability have somewhere to attach.
articles.tieback: Once agents can hold something close to legal standing to negotiate and pay suppliers, the retailers and brands they transact with will need catalogs, inventory, and order data structured for machine consumption now, which is the same problem Logicbroker's transactionable data model for LLMs and agents is built to solve.

articles.title: Kohl's debuts AI shopping assistant
articles.author: Tatiana Walk-Morris
articles.summary: Kohl's expanded its Mother's Day Gift Finder into a full AI shopping assistant built on Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise, letting shoppers get personalized recommendations, compare products, track orders, and get help with buy-online-pickup-in-store through conversational queries. The move follows similar assistants already live at Macy's, Michaels, and Lowe's.
articles.tieback: Assistants like this are only as good as the order and inventory data behind them, and for retailers running large dropship or 3P assortments, that means the same real-time visibility and automated EDI feeds Logicbroker provides so a chatbot's answer about stock or order status is actually correct.

articles.title: How Walmart uses AI to limit weather disruptions in its supply chain
articles.author: Max Garland
articles.summary: Walmart uses predictive AI models that combine historical weather patterns with real-time data to reposition inventory, adjust transit times, and reroute shipments before storms or wildfires hit. An SVP told Supply Chain Dive the models also factor in shifting customer demand, like umbrella purchases ahead of rain, to decide where to send stock.
articles.tieback: This kind of proactive rerouting only works if a retailer has current visibility into supplier-level inventory positions across its network, the same real-time order and inventory data and intelligent routing analytics that Logicbroker centralizes for retailers managing many dropship and 3P vendors.

articles.title: Cup Noodles maker taps AI to sharpen planning, reduce costs
articles.author: Phil Neuffer
articles.summary: Nissin Foods is rolling out an AI-powered demand and supply planning tool from Blue Yonder to improve forecasting accuracy, increase fill rates, and cut inventory levels as part of a broader digital transformation. The company expects the shift to also reduce reliance on capital-intensive infrastructure in favor of more predictable operating costs.
